storyboard.claim: Luther's only link to Diem's survival is the spinning compass.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther studies the golden compass, its needle spinning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the compass spinning in the dead zone of Curial.
storyboard.addedInformation: The compass is his only tether to Diem, not a navigation tool.

storyboard.claim: The bond keeps Luther bound: a spinning compass means Diem is trapped, a still one means she is free.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther bound by the bond, thinking about the compass needle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the needle matters to Luther.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains show the bond itself as a restraint, not devotion.

storyboard.claim: A tiny spinning piece of metal now dictates a general's state of mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther holds the compass up, the needle spinning uselessly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the bond logic: if she dies, he is gone too.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the absurdity: a commander's mind is governed by a compass.

storyboard.claim: The romantic reading is the instinct the hosts are about to reject.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther in thought, the romantic reading struck through on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the romance reading the hosts will challenge.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the romance as the wrong instinct, not the message.

explainedBy: Luther slumps over the compass, shown unable to function without Diem: dependence, not romance.

storyboard.claim: Luther cannot function without Diem
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther slumped, sad, holding the compass
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the tragic romance trope the host describes
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the trope is named by the callout, the slump shows the dependence

storyboard.claim: The hosts question whether the bond is really romance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther mid-speech, the question posed on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the romance reading into a question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the coming argument as a challenge to the reading.

storyboard.claim: The romance is stripped away by the lack of choice in the bond.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther in thought, the lack of choice named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question of whether the bond is romantic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Choice, not affection, is the key variable the hosts name.

storyboard.claim: His godhood overrides his free will.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther standing tense, a look of fear, the words on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the lack of choice in the bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fear shows a man overtaken, not a man loving someone.

storyboard.claim: Luther strains his own mind to hold off the magic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther slumped, straining, afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the cost of the possession on Luther.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump and fear show strain, not fondness.

storyboard.claim: The bond is a terrifying possession, not romance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther bound by chains, afraid, as the word possession appears.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the romance reading with a horror reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read as bound and controlled, the literal meaning of possession.

explainedBy: Without the glamour, Luther is shown as a risk: a worried man who is now a liability.

storyboard.claim: Without romance, Luther is a dangerous liability
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther, worried, thinking
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the possession reading
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: liability is a judgment carried by the callout

storyboard.claim: The bond compromises Luther's loyalty to the war effort.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, the war icon beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the personal bond to the wider war.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the stakes for the war, beyond Luther alone.

storyboard.claim: If Diem dies, Luther's magic would burn his own army down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fire over an army, Luther afraid beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the risk of the bond to the army.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire is literal: his magic burning his own side.

explainedBy: Luther's allegiance is bound to Diem's life, not the realm: his loyalty follows her heartbeat.

storyboard.claim: His allegiance follows Diem's heartbeat, not the realm
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther, worried, standing
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the war is compromised
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the heartbeat is a metaphor carried by the callout, not a heart icon

storyboard.claim: The scene moves back to the coast of Arboros, to Teller.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shore of Arboros, Teller sitting in the sand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Changes location from Luther to Teller on the beach.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the second story thread on the coast.

storyboard.claim: Teller sits alone on a boulder, holding a fishing rod.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller alone on the shore, sad, sitting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Teller on the beach.
storyboard.addedInformation: Solitude shows his grief, the boulder is just where he sits.

explainedBy: Teller points at the rod he crafted: a makeshift stick and horsehair fishing rod.

storyboard.claim: The rod is crafted from a stick and horsehair
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller, sad, pointing at the rod
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues Teller's introduction
storyboard.addedInformation: The rod's makeshift craft is the callout

storyboard.claim: Sor, the obsidian lumnos beside him, lets out restless whines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller seated on the shore, uneasy, Sor beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the lumnos beside Teller.
storyboard.addedInformation: The unease shows in Teller and the animal, the callout names the sound.

storyboard.claim: Teller is boiling with fury and violently hurls a ceramic jar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller, angry, fuming on the sand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates Teller from sorrow to rage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Anger shows the outburst before the jar lands.

explainedBy: The callout labels the jar's contents: a scarlet balm that smells of citrus and smoke.
noVisual: No balm or jar in the vocabulary; the callout carries the object

storyboard.claim: The jar holds the flame root balm
storyboard.concreteVisual: Empty frame with the balm label
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Says what was inside the jar
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the balm is text-led

storyboard.claim: Battle tools are forged from our most intimate familial traumas.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller, sad, the trauma phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises Teller's jar to a wider rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the war tool to family pain, the thread of the next beats.

callout.text: the exact thing that hurt you

explainedBy: Teller, slumped, stands for the person whose survival tool is the thing that hurt them most.

storyboard.claim: The thing you need to survive is what hurt you most
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller, sad, slumped
storyboard.onScreenText: the exact thing that hurt you
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the jar's trauma to the viewer
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the general 'you' is text-led

storyboard.claim: To understand the jar, we look at Teller's mother Arley.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller thinking about his mother, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the mother who is the source of the trauma.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names Arley on screen so the mother is identified.

storyboard.claim: Teller's mother manipulated him; Teller explains it to Luther.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller slumped, sad, Luther beside him; a puppeteer icon for control.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the manipulation the wording of the revelation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer shows one person controlling others from behind.

storyboard.claim: Arley secretly copied Teller's school notes when he was young.
storyboard.concreteVisual: School notes as the icon, Teller worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the first concrete example of the manipulation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes show the betrayal in literal terms.

storyboard.claim: Imagine a kid already an outcast at school, doing homework.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller, sad, the outcast phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the boy at school under the betrayal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the loneliness that makes the theft worse.

storyboard.claim: Teller's mother was weaponizing his school notes to plot a military attack.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller holding notes, war icon as the plot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates the notes from homework to war planning.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon shows the notes serve a military plot.

storyboard.claim: She was not checking homework; she was spying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller holding a magnifier, worried, reconnaissance on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Negates the homework reading with the spy reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magnifier shows scrutiny and spying, not study.

storyboard.claim: She denied Teller the choice to learn magic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door shut, Teller sad beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds a second harm to the manipulation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door shows a path closed off for Teller.

storyboard.claim: Arley used her children's mundane lives as a shield and resource.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon, Teller worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the manipulation of her children.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield shows children protecting the mother's plan.

explainedBy: The chess knight shows Arley's strategy: the host respects her as a tactician.

storyboard.claim: Arley is respected as a general
storyboard.concreteVisual: Game icon, Arley smirking
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the tactician reading to be tested
storyboard.addedInformation: The knight reads as strategy

storyboard.claim: Arley is a cold, brilliant, calculated tactician who made the impossible choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther pointing at the board, the tactician phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the host's case for Arley as a strategist.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point gesture is the board she plays.

storyboard.claim: Arley used her own children as pawns for the guardians' advantage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther, angry, pointing; a puppeteer icon for control.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the host's strategist argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer shows control over others, which is the pawn idea.

storyboard.claim: The text contradicts the idea of Arley as a cold, rational tactician.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther pointing, the tactician phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns against the strategist reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the reading as the hosts' claim.

storyboard.claim: At the truce meeting, the descended crowns offer a ceasefire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther surprised at the table, the ceasefire on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the meeting the hosts mention.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stage is the temple setting of the truce.

storyboard.claim: The mortal rebellion has fought for the ceasefire over centuries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, the centuries phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what the ceasefire means to the rebellion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the stake of the offer.

storyboard.claim: Arley rejects the ceasefire flat because of Ignos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther angry, pointing at the refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the refusal that answers the ceasefire.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point marks the rejection as her act.

storyboard.claim: Arley demands the crowns burn their ancient thrones for peace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fire icon, Luther angry while talking about the demand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains her reason: Ignos killed her daughter.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fire is the literal demand to burn the thrones.

storyboard.claim: That is not a calculated military maneuver; it is raw maternal rage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, the maneuver phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the strategist reading from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected reading; the rage is the claim.

storyboard.claim: Arley is a grieving mother who commands an army, not a chess master.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller slumped, sad, the war icon behind the grieving phrase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the debate: she is grieving, not calculating.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon shows the army she commands out of grief.
